note: Traces architectural evolution through to multimodal models and compares them on technical features rather than marketing claims.
title: Survey of Different Large Language Model Architectures: Trends, Benchmarks, and Challenges
explain_beginner: This survey traces how large language models, the AI systems behind tools like ChatGPT, have evolved architecturally and compares the main families side by side rather than repeating marketing claims. It groups models into three broad design types, ones built to understand text deeply like BERT, ones built to generate text by predicting the next word like the GPT and LLaMA families, and ones built to transform one text into another like translation style models such as T5. It also covers the newer category of multimodal models that handle images and audio alongside text. Rather than just listing model names, the authors evaluate them against a shared set of standard tests covering reading comprehension, common sense, and science questions, so readers can compare capability rather than hype. The paper's value is organizational, helping someone new to the field understand what family a given model belongs to and what that implies, though it does not itself introduce a new model or method.
explain_business: For a team choosing between model families for a new product, this survey's three way architecture split, understanding focused, generation focused, and transformation focused, plus the newer multimodal category, is a practical filter for narrowing vendor and open source options to the right shape of tool before evaluating specific products. Because the comparisons are grounded in named public benchmarks like MMLU and SuperGLUE rather than vendor claims, procurement teams can request the same benchmark scores from vendors to make an apples to apples comparison instead of relying on marketing language. The authors' identification of data scarcity, context window limits, and multimodal alignment as still open technical problems is useful for setting realistic expectations with stakeholders, since promises of unlimited context or seamless image plus text reasoning from any vendor should be verified against these known limitations rather than accepted at face value.
explain_practitioner: This survey categorizes LLM architectures into three families, auto encoding models such as BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa built for contextual understanding, auto regressive models such as the GPT series, LLaMA, and PaLM built for left to right generation, and sequence to sequence models such as T5 and BART built around encoder decoder designs for conditional generation, then extends the comparison to multimodal systems like KOSMOS-1. Model comparisons are grounded in standard benchmarks including MMLU's 57 subject areas, SuperGLUE, HellaSwag, ARC, and WinoGrande for language understanding and reasoning, plus VQA and NLVR2 for cross modal tasks. The authors identify concrete unresolved challenges rather than only celebrating progress, specifically that high quality training data is becoming scarce as models scale, that context window limits and catastrophic forgetting during continual learning remain unsolved, and that cross modal alignment between text and images is still technically difficult to achieve reliably, all flagged as open problems rather than solved by any surveyed architecture.
